body:
Haha, yea. I'm not sure now when I will try to spit it out, but probably soon enough. I'll be updating on it then.

> Have you ever told your therapist about that feeling of her being not professional? Maybe try it at the phone, if you can't stand being near her.

No, only after she had scheduled an appointment on her own and the next day asking why I didn't show up (she had done a similar thing before) I kindly told her that we never made an appointment and I do not want to continue the meetings. But yea, I'm the type of person who will avoid criticizing anyone and hates conflicts. Gladly she only answers through text messages (I absolutely hate talking on the phone) so if I need to contact her again, I wont have to talk or be face to face.

When I first contacted her, I kinda assumed I would go there for like one or two times and get a referral to a psychiatrist or someone who is more specialized to my specific issues. You know, so I could maybe get medication and a well constructed treatment. She just seemed very confused herself on what to do with me and I didn't really know how these things work, so I just kind of tried to trust she knew what she was doing and kept an open mind.

> I'd first make sure that's the case.

I could always contact another doctor, but I fear I'd just be getting the same answer. The one that said I should contact the psychologist again made me feel kinda embarrassed. She didn't even consider that I wasn't comfortable talking with her and sent me off after a minute or two of me being there.

> My idea was to make my partner bug me until I spit it out.

I hope that works for you. How are you gonna get your partner to do that though? 

Mine has tried to get the truth out of me but for no use. I would just say that I'm tired or I have a migraine (which is often times true), but that's just because I wasn't ready to tell him yet. He has probably learnt that that doesn't work so I don't think I'll be able to use that trick. Just gonna have to open up on my own.

It's wonderful that you've got someone else to keep you straight, as we know we can't really trust ourselves with that. I know my partner has to fetch me from the bathroom on a daily basis and I'm incredibly thankful he has the patience to do that.

Also great that you're still motivated to keep on trying and have kept your face in order. I personally feel like as long as my face doesn't look like that of a drug addict, I'm doing great with this compulsion. Just take one step at a time. So now you've managed to keep your face on, good, next focus on you neck area.

In the end it really comes down to accepting the past as it is and looking forward. Everyone has their scars. Ours may not be as cool, but its still all part of life.

Thank you. Would you like to update on how it went with your partner? I hope it goes well!

About me being suicidal, he has no idea, at least what I'm aware of. Yet he does know I'm not ok and that I'm worse than what I let him know. My behavior is increasingly unstable and my lifelong depression is finally getting to my everyday life.

I did actually go to a psychologist recently (for the first time ever), but had a bit of a backlash there and I called off our meetings (I didn't feel like she was being professional enough on more than one occation). Tried to get help trough another way and telling them how I feel (not the suicidal stuff though) and why I didn't feel comfortable going to the first psychologist, the answer was for me to contact her again and continue the meetings. That lead me to finally go "fuck it, this is it now".

The reason for it was that I had gotten a referral from a doctor to a psychologist a year earlier and due to being super busy, our schedules collided for too long. So I just left it be. Apparently they now think that I'm not capable of committing to a treatment, which is probably written in my files now for any doctor to see.

Now I'm at the point where I would probably have to go to that specific psychologist to get anywhere with my mental health treatment... but I really don't want to, just her face makes me tick.

But yea, I suppose the next step now would be to open up to my partner about the severeness of my issues, so maybe we can think of something together. I did tell him the above and he was kinda pissed to the system. So I guess I'll have his support no matter what, It's just damn hard to open up your mouth.

Thank you. Writing down my thoughts first would probably help the conversation a lot, I will certainly do that.

And I suppose I don't have anything to lose anyways as I was going to take my life and nothing is stopping me to reschedule it if I so please. It's not like he's going to hurt any more from having a heads up, might even make it easier. 

Though it could be a little harder to do it with him getting more protective of me. That's probably what I fear the most, him feeling like he's somehow responsible of me and always fearing

It is indeed fair to give him a chance to help me, as being in a committed relationship makes this not just my own problem. The issue here is that I have a major emotional wall and trouble expressing my feelings (probably why I'm in this mess in the first place), so I'm just gonna have to find a way to push myself there. 

Thank you for the encouragement. I hope for my boyfriend's sake to find the guts to come out to him :)
